preceding_agent.observed_effect: Explicit highest-value frontier selection changed the search allocation toward more informative flow: the opportunistic era concentrated ~10 activations on repeated robustness dimensions of one signal class (MA crossover), whereas the frontier-first/controller era closed 6+ distinct signal-class cells once each with decisive, independently verified verdicts and no equivalent re-tests, and surfaced the first positive candidate (momentum, SUPPORTED) that queue-following had not reached. Information diversity and decisiveness per activation increased.

preceding_agent.research_result: No new research result (process audit only). Finding: explicit highest-value selection is associated with more diverse, decisive, non-duplicative information flow in the durable record; no observed bottleneck justifies changing the selector.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: Partially reduced: durable evidence establishes a behavioral contrast (diversified, decisive, non-duplicative cell closure under explicit selection vs concentrated single-class refinement under the queue), supporting a concrete selection advantage at the search-allocation level; clean causal isolation and the current controller selector's own end-to-end effect remain open.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_targeted: Whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection improves learning efficiency (information gained per activation) relative to the repository's prior opportunistic queue-driven task choice.
unverified: No controlled counterfactual exists: the opportunistic and frontier-first eras differ in wall-clock time, toolkit maturity, and worker session, so the improvement cannot be cleanly isolated to the selector alone (toolkit maturation co-occurred, though it is orthogonal to which hypothesis is selected).
